body_markdown:
When we moved into our new Littleton headquarters earlier this year, it was about more than just square footage. It was a physical marker of a broader evolution. We’ve grown from roughly 90 people to over 125 in a short window, and while the space is new, the mission remains the same: solving problems that most of the world doesn’t even know exist yet.


At


[Precision Optics](https://www.poci.com/) , we often describe ourselves as a “40-year-old startup.” It’s an accurate way to view how we operate. We have the deep institutional knowledge and long-term history you can’t manufacture overnight, but we carry the agility and hunger of a company that’s just getting started.


## It Starts in the Lab


When people ask what makes us different, we point them to the Lab. We’ve rebranded our micro-optics division to


[The Lab at Precision Optics](https://www.poci.com/blogs/inside-the-lab-at-precision-optics-corporation-turning-complex-designs-into-real-systems/) , but the work happening there hasn’t changed, it’s been refined over decades.


In an industry that is increasingly obsessed with automation, we lean into artisanship.


When a customer brings us a design that seems impossible to prototype, something that might be too intricate for a standard CNC optical shop, that’s when we’re at our best. Our team doesn’t just look at CAD models; they have the “old-school” optical engineering hands that know how to troubleshoot the nuances of glass and assembly.


That human element is our secret sauce.


It’s what allows us to produce sub-100-micron components that work, reliably, the first time.


## Grounding the AI Hype


You can’t talk about optics in 2026 without talking about AI and data integration. Everyone is looking for the “AI-driven solution.”


From our perspective, if you don’t have a solid physical foundation, AI is just noise. You cannot rely on software to patch a poor mechanical interface. We look at AI as a fine-tuning element. It’s a powerful tool to process massive amounts of fluorescence or near-IR data, but it requires a robust, high-quality imaging chain to be effective.


Our job is to build the architecture that gives those algorithms the cleanest data possible. When we provide that foundation, the AI works better. The device works better. The surgeon gets a better outcome.


## The “Partnership” is the Product


We’ve found that the best products don’t come from a customer handing us a spec sheet and saying, “build this.” They come from a collaborative process.


Sometimes that means we have to have tough conversations. We have to look at a design and say, “That’s a brilliant idea, but operationally, it needs to be approached differently.” We help customers navigate the “gotchas” of FDA and ITAR regulations, which can be an intimidating landscape for early-stage companies. We aren’t just selling parts; we’re selling a path to commercialization.


As we look at the next three to five years, the trajectory is clear. We’re seeing a shift where traditional, reusable medical devices are moving toward single-use. We’re scaling our team and our equipment to meet that demand.


We’re growing, we’re hiring, and we’re continuing to do the work that others find too difficult to tackle.


Whether you’re a startup looking to get to your first prototype or an established firm iterating on your third generation, we’re ready to get to work.


Let’s see what we can build next!
